functions.name: containsPattern
functions.doc: `%q%` for ILIKE, with q's own wildcards escaped.

functions.name: fuzzy
functions.doc: Typo-tolerant match on a trigram-indexed column (users.username, topics.name): similar words via pg_trgm's `%`, or a plain substring.

functions.name: paperQuery
functions.doc: A paper query in both languages: English stemming, or the 'bangla' configuration (migration 005).

functions.name: paperRank
functions.doc: Relevance of a paper for `q`, for ordering search results.

functions.name: refreshPaperSearch
functions.doc: Rebuilds a paper's search document. Call it in the same transaction as any change to the paper's title, authors or main idea, or to its Paper Cards. The expression lives in one SQL function (refresh_paper_search, migration 005), so the backfill and the app can't disagree.

functions.name: startsWithPattern
functions.doc: `q%` for ILIKE: starts with q.

functions.name: canSeeContentOf
functions.doc: The viewer may see this user's posts and reading tracker: a visible profile that is public or followed.

functions.name: canSeeProfile
functions.doc: The viewer may open this user's profile: active and not blocked either way.

functions.name: followsOrIs
functions.doc: The viewer is the user or an accepted follower.

functions.name: isActiveUser
functions.doc: The account is active: not suspended, not deleted.

functions.name: isPublished
functions.doc: Team content (papers, courses, learn items, questions, quizzes) that is live. Drafts and archived rows are staff-only.

functions.name: isSearchablePost
functions.doc: A post that may appear in search: published, live, from a public account the viewer may see. Private posts never do.

functions.name: isVisiblePost
functions.doc: A post the viewer may see (author aliased `u`). Authors also see their own posts still processing.

functions.name: notBlocked
functions.doc: Neither the viewer nor the user (by id column) has blocked the other. An unblock keeps the row with is_active = false.

functions.name: devAuthContext
functions.doc: Development only (DEV_AUTH_BYPASS): acts as an existing active user with no token. Reuses one long-lived session per user so session-based routes (sign out, push token) still work. Counts as two-factor signed in, so staff routes open for a seeded admin.

errors.message: Dev sign-in: no active user "…". Run pnpm db:seed, or send ….

functions.name: decrypt
functions.doc: Returns null if the value was not produced by `encrypt` with the same purpose.

functions.name: encrypt
functions.doc: AES-256-GCM. Output: base64url(iv | auth tag | ciphertext).

functions.name: hashToken
functions.doc: One-way hash for secrets kept in the database (refresh tokens, email codes).

functions.name: randomToken
functions.doc: A random, URL-safe secret.

functions.name: signToken
functions.doc: A short self-contained token: base64url(JSON) + "." + HMAC. Tamper-proof, not secret. `expiresAt` is required: every signed token in this app expires.

functions.name: verifyToken
functions.doc: Returns the token's data, or null if it was tampered with or has expired.

functions.name: fetchPage
functions.doc: Runs `query` for one page, newest first by default.

functions.name: fetchRankedPage
functions.doc: Keyset pagination on a numeric rank, smallest first, then the internal id: for lists ordered by a score instead of time (the Research collection by trend rank). `rank` must be the same expression as the index it should use.

functions.name: mapPage
functions.doc: Applies `map` to every item of a page.

functions.name: generateTotpSecret
functions.doc: A new random secret, base32-encoded as authenticator apps expect.

functions.name: totpUri
functions.doc: The otpauth:// link an authenticator app reads from a QR code.

functions.name: verifyTotp
functions.doc: Accepts the current code and one step either side, to allow for clock drift.

functions.name: slugify
functions.doc: Turns a name into a slug ("Attention mechanism" → "attention-mechanism"). Empty for names with no ASCII letters.

functions.name: contentId
functions.doc: The internal id of the content row with this public id, or 404.

functions.name: contentMediaId
functions.doc: A team-content upload (purpose learn or paper_figure) by public id; undefined and null pass through.

errors.message: media_id must be an upload with purpose "learn"

functions.name: idsInOrder
functions.doc: Internal ids for public ids, in the same order. Any unknown id is a 400 naming it.

functions.name: slugToId
functions.doc: Topic or field id by slug; undefined stays undefined and null stays null (for PATCH bodies).

functions.name: syncSearch
functions.doc: Records a content change for search, when that kind of content is searchable.

functions.name: selectCourses
functions.doc: ----- Courses (drafts until published) -----

functions.name: selectItems
functions.doc: ----- Learn items (drafts until published) -----

functions.name: responsibleUserId
functions.doc: The account behind a report's target: the user itself, or the author of the post or comment.

functions.name: targetPreview
functions.doc: What a report points at, for the moderator to judge without opening the app.

functions.name: selectQuestions
functions.doc: Staff view of questions: includes answers, explanations and status.

functions.name: linkTarget
functions.doc: The internal id of a learn item, quiz or live reel that a prerequisite links to, as the matching column.

functions.name: selectPapers
functions.doc: Staff view of papers: every status, with who changed them last. Same response shape as before migration 006. Left joins on the companions, so a paper that somehow lacks them still shows here.

functions.name: splitPaperBody
functions.doc: Splits a paper body by where each field is stored: the papers row, paper_metadata (doi, arxiv_id) and the English Paper Card (the Prototype 2 summary). Fields left out stay undefined, which Kysely skips, so a PATCH changes only what was sent.

functions.name: writeSummaryToCard
functions.doc: Writes summary fields from a paper body to the English card, creating it if needed.

functions.name: availableUsername
functions.doc: A free username based on the email's local part, for accounts created through Google.

functions.name: completeMfaLogin
functions.doc: Second step for accounts with two-factor sign-in.

functions.name: confirmPasswordReset
functions.doc: Sets the new password and signs out every device.

functions.name: consumeAuthToken
functions.doc: Marks a one-time code used and returns its user, or throws if it is unknown, used or expired.

functions.name: login
functions.doc: Email or username plus password. Every failure looks the same, so it can't reveal which accounts exist.

functions.name: refresh
functions.doc: Swaps a refresh token for a new pair. Each refresh token works once. If an old one comes back, someone copied it, so the whole session is revoked.

functions.name: requestPasswordReset
functions.doc: Always succeeds, so the response can't reveal whether an account uses that email.

functions.name: setPushToken
functions.doc: Stores this device's push token (FCM), or clears it with null.

functions.name: signInWithGoogle
functions.doc: Google sign-in. The ID token is verified by providers.google. An existing Google link signs in; otherwise a verified Google email links to the account with that email, or creates a new one.

errors.message: Google sign-in could not be verified

functions.name: enableTwoFactor
functions.doc: Step 2: the first code from the app proves it was set up correctly.

functions.name: setupTwoFactor
functions.doc: Step 1: a new secret for the authenticator app. Nothing changes until `enable` confirms a code.

functions.name: addComment
functions.doc: Adds a comment, or a reply with `parentId`. Counting and notifications happen in the worker.

errors.message: You can only reply to a comment in the same thread

functions.name: deleteComment
functions.doc: Soft delete: the comment becomes a "[deleted]" placeholder. Authors can delete their own.

errors.message: You can only delete your own comments

functions.name: listComments
functions.doc: Top-level comments, oldest first. Replies are fetched per comment.

functions.name: resolveThread
functions.doc: The internal ids of a thread the viewer may see: a visible post or a published paper.

functions.name: selectComments
functions.doc: Comments the viewer may see. A deleted comment, or one whose author is gone or suspended, stays as a "[deleted]" placeholder (body and author null) so its replies keep their place. Comments by someone the viewer blocked, or who blocked the viewer, are left out.

functions.name: visibleComment
functions.doc: A comment whose thread the viewer may see (live or deleted), or 404.

functions.name: completeLearnItem
functions.doc: Marks a published lesson or note as completed, wherever it was opened.

functions.name: getCourse
functions.doc: A course with its published learn items in step order.

functions.name: listMyCourses
functions.doc: Courses the viewer has started, most recent first: "continue where you left off".

functions.name: markTopicKnown
functions.doc: "I already know this": the topic counts as done in every paper's Learn first list.

functions.name: saveProgress
functions.doc: Records the step the viewer reached. Reaching the last step marks the course completed.

errors.message: External courses have no steps to track

functions.name: selectCourses
functions.doc: Published courses (ours and external cards), with the viewer's progress.

functions.name: selectLearnItems
functions.doc: Published learn items with their topic and media.

functions.name: toLearnItem
functions.doc: A learn item. `media` is a file from the upload pipeline; `media_url` is an outside link the team pasted instead. An item has at most one of them.

functions.name: topicRef
functions.doc: `{ slug, name }` of the topic aliased `t`, or null when the item has no topic.

functions.name: completeUpload
functions.doc: Step 2: the app says the upload finished. The file must exist with the declared size. The asset then waits as `processing`, which is the worker's queue.

errors.message: Uploaded file size does not match the declared size

functions.name: createUpload
functions.doc: Step 1 of an upload: checks the declared file, records the asset as `uploading`, and returns a short-lived URL the app uploads the bytes to directly. The bytes never pass through the API.

errors.message: Only admins can upload team content

functions.name: getOwnMedia
functions.doc: The owner's view of an asset, including the error when processing failed.

functions.name: maxBytes
functions.doc: Largest upload per kind and purpose. Learn videos run minutes, reels at most 90 seconds.

functions.name: mediaView
functions.doc: Builds the URLs for an asset. Keys under "public/" get plain cacheable URLs. Post media gets signed URLs: valid about a day for public accounts (so CDNs can cache them), one to two hours for private ones.

functions.name: signedUrlExpiry
functions.doc: Rounded up to the next hour or day, so the same URL repeats and stays cacheable within that window.

functions.name: withMediaView
functions.doc: Replaces a row's media_* columns with one `media` object.

functions.name: listNotifications
functions.doc: Newest first. `paper_id` is set for replies in a paper discussion, so the app can open the paper.

functions.name: selectNotifications
functions.doc: Alerts whose actor is still active and not blocked either way.

functions.name: createPost
functions.doc: Text posts need a caption. Image and reel posts need the id of an upload the author completed (POST /v1/media/:id/complete). If that upload is still processing, the post waits as "processing" and the worker publishes it, with a "your post is live" notification.

functions.name: deletePost
functions.doc: Soft delete: the post disappears now; the worker removes it and its media after the grace period.

errors.message: You can only delete your own posts

functions.name: likePost
functions.doc: A like is one row per user and post, toggled with `is_active`: unliking keeps the row, and liking again flips it back. An event is written only when the state really changes, and only the first like ever notifies the author. Counting and notifying happen in the worker.

functions.name: listFeed
functions.doc: Home: published posts by people the viewer follows (accepted), newest first.

functions.name: listReels
functions.doc: Newest reels the viewer may see. Ranking by engagement waits for Redis and watch data.

functions.name: selectPosts
functions.doc: Posts the viewer may see, with author, media, stored counters and the viewer's like and save.

functions.name: toPost
functions.doc: The API shape of a post. Media URLs are signed for 1–2 hours when the author's account is private.

functions.name: visiblePost
functions.doc: The internal id and author of a post the viewer may see, or 404.

functions.name: checkAnswer
functions.doc: Checks an answer and records the attempt for the user's practice history.

functions.name: getStats
functions.doc: Accuracy per topic and overall, and the streak of consecutive days with practice.

functions.name: listQuestions
functions.doc: Random questions from one topic, or from all for "Random".

functions.name: normalize
functions.doc: Short answers match regardless of case and extra spaces.

functions.name: selectQuestions
functions.doc: Published questions as the app shows them: never with the answer or explanation.

functions.name: streakDays
functions.doc: Consecutive local days (APP_TIMEZONE) with at least one answer, ending today or yesterday.

functions.name: createReport
functions.doc: Files a report for the moderation queue. Reporting the same thing twice keeps one open report.

functions.name: targetId
functions.doc: Resolves what a user may report to its internal id. reports.target_id has no foreign key (it points at users, posts, comments or trails, and must outlive its target), so this is where a target is checked: it exists in the table its type names, and the reporter may see it. user    an active account other than the reporter's own (blocked users can still be reported) post    a post the reporter can see comment a live comment in a thread the reporter can see (also by someone the reporter blocked) trail   a published trail the reporter can see, or their own

functions.name: createPaperCompanions
functions.doc: Creates a paper's three one-to-one companion rows (migration 006). Call it in the transaction that inserts the paper: lists and the ingestion queue join them, so a paper without them would not be listed or synced. `ids` are the identifiers known up front (an import, or staff input).

functions.name: getLearnFirst
functions.doc: Learn first: the paper's prerequisite concepts in order. Each has a label, why it matters, and a typed link to our own lesson, note, quiz or reel. `done` is computed: the linked lesson or note is completed, every question of the linked quiz has been answered, or the user said "I already know this". The Prototype 2 shape (each topic with all its learn items) is kept alongside.

functions.name: getLineage
functions.doc: A6, lineage: the published papers this one builds on (it cites them) and the notable ones that built on it (they cite it), influential citations first, then most cited. Each carries the citation intent; `contrasting` ("this later paper disputes this result") is set by staff.

functions.name: getPaper
functions.doc: The paper screen: the Prototype 2 structured summary (same keys as before, now read from the English card), the Paper Card in each language it exists in, scholarly metadata, the links to open the original (A10; we never host a PDF) and the viewer's own reading pass with their private note.

functions.name: getReadingTracker
functions.doc: A user's tracker for their profile, grouped by status. Like their posts, a private account's tracker is empty to anyone but accepted followers.

functions.name: getRelatedPapers
functions.doc: "Papers like this one": published papers ranked by how many Learn first topics they share, then same field, then newest. Semantic similarity replaces this when Elasticsearch arrives.

functions.name: getResearchOutput
functions.doc: Reopens a saved output from the stored row: no AI call, nothing counted against an allowance.

functions.name: getRoadmap
functions.doc: A field's starting roadmap: published papers in reading order, numbered 1..n, each with a note.

functions.name: getUpNext
functions.doc: "Up next" on the Research home: the earliest saved paper the user hasn't marked read.

functions.name: getUserReadingStats
functions.doc: Profile → Reading. Like posts and the tracker, a private account's counts are for accepted followers only.

functions.name: listFields
functions.doc: The topic chips, in their fixed order (ML fundamentals → … → Emerging research).

functions.name: listMyPapers
functions.doc: My papers: `saved` (saved, not read yet, newest saved first) or `read` (step ≥ 1, latest first).

functions.name: listPapers
functions.doc: The collection. Default order is the trend rank the worker keeps (A1). `q` searches title, authors and the card question in English and Bangla (A2). `interests: true` keeps the viewer's onboarding fields.

functions.name: listResearchOutputs
functions.doc: My papers → Maps and roadmaps: saved AI outputs, newest first, without their (large) result.

functions.name: readingCounts
functions.doc: How many papers reached each step, this month (APP_TIMEZONE) and in total. Steps are cumulative.

functions.name: savedUnread
functions.doc: Saved papers not yet read (no step 1).

functions.name: selectPaperCards
functions.doc: Published papers as lists show them: metadata from ingestion (venue, TLDR, citations, Hugging Face upvotes, trend rank, New badge), the card question in both languages, and the viewer's save, reading step and Prototype 2 tracker status (`my_status`, kept as it was).

functions.name: setPaperNote
functions.doc: The private note (at most 400 characters; null clears it). Only its owner ever reads it.

functions.name: setPaperStatus
functions.doc: Save (status "saved"), or move along the tracker to "reading" and "completed".

functions.name: setReadingStep
functions.doc: Sets the reading step. `exact` lets the user move to any step, including back down (later step times are cleared); `at_least` only raises it, for the one-tap "Mark read" (step 1).

functions.name: summaryFromEnglishCard
functions.doc: The Prototype 2 summary fields, read from the English Paper Card (left-joined as `en`), which is their only home since migration 006. research_questions is the card question followed by its extra questions.

functions.name: search
functions.doc: One search box: the top matches of each type, grouped. Pass `types` to fetch only some ("See all").

functions.name: suggest
functions.doc: Autocomplete while typing: a few names and titles that start with (or contain) the text. The app calls it 250 ms after the last keystroke, from 2 characters.

errors.message: You can only delete your own trails

functions.name: getTrail
functions.doc: A trail with its published papers in order, numbered 1..n, each with the author's note.

functions.name: listTrails
functions.doc: Published trails, newest first, optionally for one chip or language (Research and Learn).

functions.name: listUserTrails
functions.doc: A user's trails: published ones, plus drafts and removed ones when it is the viewer's own list.

functions.name: ownTrail
functions.doc: The viewer's own trail, for changes. 404 if it doesn't exist, 403 if it is someone else's.

errors.message: You can only change your own trails
A trail needs at least … papers before it is published

functions.name: setTrailStatus
functions.doc: Publish or move back to draft. `removed` is a moderator's decision and can't be set here.

functions.name: visibleTrailId
functions.doc: The internal id of a trail the viewer may see (for reports), or 404.

functions.name: writeItems
functions.doc: Replaces the trail's steps. Only published papers can be added.

functions.name: userSummary
functions.doc: `{ id, username, display_name, avatar_url }` for the user aliased `table`, with the public id as `id`.

functions.name: block
functions.doc: Blocks a user: hides each from the other everywhere, and ends follows in both directions.

functions.name: declineFollowRequest
functions.doc: The row stays as 'inactive', so a repeated request from the same person doesn't notify again.

functions.name: deleteAccount
functions.doc: Starts account deletion: the account disappears at once and every session ends. The worker purges its data after ACCOUNT_PURGE_DAYS. Password accounts must confirm with the password.

functions.name: endFollow
functions.doc: Ends a follow or a pending request, keeping the row as 'inactive'. Ending an accepted follow moves the stored counts. Does nothing if there is no live follow.

functions.name: follow
functions.doc: Follows a public account, or sends a follow request to a private one.

functions.name: getAccount
functions.doc: The signed-in user's own account. password_hash and totp_secret are never selected outside auth.

functions.name: getInterests
functions.doc: Fields picked at onboarding.

functions.name: getProfile
functions.doc: A profile page. 404 when the account is inactive or either side has blocked the other.

functions.name: listBlocks
functions.doc: The user's active blocks, most recent first by when each (re)started.

functions.name: listFollowRequests
functions.doc: Waiting requests, newest first by when they were (re)sent.

functions.name: suggestUsers
functions.doc: People to follow on an empty Home: the most-followed active users the viewer has no follow or request with. Reads users_suggest_idx in order, so no user's followers are counted here.

functions.name: suspendUser
functions.doc: Suspends an account and signs it out everywhere. Used by moderation and admins.

functions.name: unblock
functions.doc: Ends a block, keeping the row with is_active = false. Does nothing if there is no active block.

functions.name: unfollow
functions.doc: Unfollows, or withdraws a pending request.

functions.name: visibleUserId
functions.doc: The internal id of a user the viewer may see, or 404.

functions.name: cleanUp
functions.doc: Abandoned uploads, ended sessions, used codes and old processed events.

functions.name: purgeDeletedAccounts
functions.doc: Accounts deleted more than ACCOUNT_PURGE_DAYS ago lose their data. Their comments stay as "[deleted]" placeholders with the text erased, so other people's reply threads survive.

functions.name: purgeDeletedPosts
functions.doc: Posts their authors deleted are removed for good, with their media, after the same grace period.

functions.name: rankCollection
functions.doc: Keeps the Research order current for newly published papers, even with ingestion switched off.

functions.name: repairCounters
functions.doc: Repairs stored counts that drifted from the real rows. The worker moves counts by ±1 per event; drift comes from paths that emit no event, mainly account purges (cascaded likes and follows, blanked comments).

functions.name: processedPrefix
functions.doc: Where an asset's processed files live. Post media is private (signed URLs); the rest is public.

functions.name: processNextMedia
functions.doc: Processes the oldest waiting asset. Returns false when the queue is empty.

functions.name: notify
functions.doc: Records an in-app notification and returns the push to send after commit. Skips alerts for your own actions (except "post ready"), for inactive recipients, and between users who blocked each other.

functions.name: pushToUser
functions.doc: Sends to every signed-in device of the user that registered a push token.

functions.name: bumpPostCounter
functions.doc: Moves a stored post counter by one. O(1), unlike recounting every like on a busy post. Safe because each event is claimed and applied exactly once (see processOutboxBatch); the hourly repair job fixes any drift from other paths, such as account purges.

functions.name: createAuthToken
functions.doc: A one-time code. Only its hash is stored; the plain code exists only in the email.

functions.name: handlers.comment.created
functions.doc: A reply notifies the parent's author; any comment on a post also notifies the post's author.

functions.name: handlers.comment.deleted
functions.doc: Written only when a live comment becomes deleted, so it is taken off exactly once.

functions.name: handlers.follow.created
functions.doc: Written only for the first follow ever between two people, so re-follows don't re-notify.

functions.name: handlers.media.ready
functions.doc: Publishes posts waiting on this media, or makes it the owner's avatar.

functions.name: handlers.post.liked
functions.doc: Counts every like that became active; notifies only for the first like ever (not a re-like).

functions.name: handlers.search.sync
functions.doc: Kept for the Elasticsearch indexer, which doesn't exist yet: nothing to do for now.

functions.name: processOutboxBatch
functions.doc: Handles pending events in order. Each event is first claimed (marked processed only if it still isn't), then handled, in one transaction: its database work and its mark commit together or not at all, and a second worker that picked the same event finds it claimed and skips it. That is what makes counter deltas safe. Push and email run after the commit. Returns how many events were picked up.

functions.name: intentOf
functions.doc: Semantic Scholar labels a citation background, methodology or result. We keep those labels and map them onto ours without guessing: methodology (the paper builds on the cited method) is supporting, background is background, and result alone stays unknown, because it can support or dispute. Contrasting is only ever set by staff.

functions.name: rankPapers
functions.doc: The default Research order, 1..n over published papers: papers trending on Hugging Face in the last PAPER_TRENDING_DAYS first (most upvoted first), then by citation count, then newest.

functions.name: replaceEdges
functions.doc: Rewrites the paper's outgoing edges to papers in our collection. Staff edges are never changed.

functions.name: runPaperSync
functions.doc: One round of the worker's papers loop: trending data every 6 hours, then a batch of papers that are new or due a refresh, then the trend ranking if anything changed. Returns true while papers are waiting, so the loop goes again without sleeping.

functions.name: syncDuePapers
functions.doc: Papers never synced (imports, or "sync now") first, then the stalest.

functions.name: syncPaper
functions.doc: Fetches one paper from OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar and stores what it found. Descriptive fields (title, authors, venue, abstract…) are only filled when empty, so staff edits win; counts, TLDR and ids are refreshed every time. References become paper_edges.

functions.name: syncTrending
functions.doc: Hugging Face daily papers for the last week: upvotes, the day a paper was listed, and its code repo, for papers in our collection (matched by arXiv id). Returns how many papers it updated.

events.name: follow.created
events.doc: entity: the followed user. Only the first follow (or request) ever between the two: it notifies.

events.name: follow.changed
events.doc: entity: the followed user. An accepted follow began (+1) or ended (-1): moves both stored counts.

events.name: post.liked
events.doc: entity: post. Written only when a like actually becomes active. `first_like` is false for a re-like, which counts but doesn't notify. Events from before migration 004 lack it: treat as true.

events.name: post.unliked
events.doc: entity: post. Written only when an active like is undone.

events.name: media.ready
events.doc: entity: media asset. The worker publishes waiting posts, sets avatars and notifies.

events.name: email.verify
events.doc: entity: user. The worker creates the one-time code (only its hash is stored) and emails it.

events.name: search.sync
events.doc: A searchable record changed (entity_type says which). No consumer yet: the Elasticsearch indexer will read these. See docs/prototype-2-implementation-notes.md.

env.name: PUBLIC_URL
env.doc: Where clients reach this server; used to build upload, media, share and email links.

env.name: APP_SECRET
env.doc: Root secret. Separate keys for tokens, cursors, signed URLs and 2FA secrets are derived from it.

env.name: GOOGLE_CLIENT_IDS
env.doc: Google OAuth client ids whose ID tokens are accepted. Empty disables Google sign-in.

env.name: DEV_AUTH_BYPASS
env.doc: Development only: requests without an Authorization header act as DEV_AUTH_USER (or the username in an `x-dev-user` header), with no sign-in and no two-factor step. Requests that do send a token still go through real auth. Refused when NODE_ENV=production.

env.name: SMTP_URL
env.doc: smtp(s)://user:pass@host:port. Empty writes emails to DEV_MAIL_DIR instead of sending them.

env.name: PAPER_SYNC_ENABLED
env.doc: Paper ingestion (worker only; the API never calls a scholarly service). OpenAlex asks clients to send a contact address for its polite pool: use a team address, never a user's. A free Semantic Scholar key raises its rate limit; without one, requests share a busy public pool.

env.name: APP_TIMEZONE
env.doc: Used to count practice streaks in the users' local days.

env.name: ANDROID_PACKAGE_NAME
env.doc: For Android App Links (/.well-known/assetlinks.json) and the Play Store fallback of share links.
